Mixed macro signals, modest policy support. The FOMC notes strong employment and robust household spending but acknowledges weak business fixed investment and exports with inflation below 2%. Empirically, investment is highly cyclical and sensitive to internal finance and uncertainty; inventory and capex slowdowns often amplify downturn risk (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994; investment as a driver of business cycles). With market-based inflation compensation low and survey expectations little changed, cutting rates aligns with New Keynesian evidence that inflation dynamics hinge on expectations (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and the case for anchoring around a symmetric 2% objective (Svensson). The rate cut and T-bill purchases/repo operations support ample reserves and smooth policy transmission, consistent with evidence that monetary policy has short-run real effects on output and rates (Sims; Zha; McCallum and Nelson) via liquidity and funding channels. Open-economy work (Lane; Engel) suggests easing can support net exports via real depreciation, though global demand likely caps the benefit. Netting positives (strong labor/consumption, policy easing) against negatives (capex/export weakness, sub-2% inflation, dissent signaling uncertainty), sentiment is cautiously positive.
